name: LegalBench
description: A collaboratively-built benchmark covering 162 legal reasoning tasks contributed by 40+ legal researchers and practitioners. Tasks span the IRAC framework (Issue spotting, Rule recall, Application, Conclusion) and include contract analysis, statutory interpretation, case identification, and procedural knowledge. Focused primarily on US law.
typical_sota_score: ~60–80% average (frontier models as of 2025; varies widely across task types)
reputation: Most comprehensive open-source legal benchmark; published at NeurIPS 2023; developed by Stanford Law and collaborators from 40+ institutions; widely cited in legal AI research; standard for US legal reasoning evaluation
notes: Published at NeurIPS 2023. 162 tasks across the IRAC legal reasoning framework from 40+ contributors. Focused on American law — international law coverage is limited. Tasks range from binary classification (yes/no) to open-ended analysis. Models still struggle with complex reasoning tasks like statute interpretation and case outcome prediction. Complemented by region-specific benchmarks (LegalBench.PT, VLegal-Bench) for other jurisdictions.
